newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: DJI CLOTHING BUYS MAJORITY STAKE IN AROMA.
newsitem.headline: DJI CLOTHING BUYS MAJORITY STAKE IN AROMA.

text.p: South African DJI Clothing Ltd said on Tuesday it is to buy a majority stake in Aroma Liquor Holdings Ltd for 7.05 million rand.
The 57.4 percent stake is to be pruchased from Aroma chairman Michael Kovensky and other directors and associated shareholders.
DJI is currently a "cash shell" company controlled by Mycom South Africa Ltd . Mycom wants to use DJI as a vehicle to buy a diversified group of industrial companies in South Africa.
"Mycom SA will be able to bring its financial backing and administrative expertise to Aroma without altering the existing management control of Aroma's experienced management team," Mycom said.
Aroma owns a series of retail drink outlets, provides management services to the drinks industry and runs a hotel operation.

Mycom is to make an offer to the remaining minority shareholders in Aroma at 87 cents a share for 57.4 percent of each minority's holding to be settled by the issue of new DJI shares at 400 cents a share.
For the remaining 42.6 percent of each minority's holding DJI will offer 125 cents a share in cash.
Aroma shares slumped on Monday after issuing a cautionary that a controlling interest in the company would be sold at a substantial discount to Friday's closing price of 224 cents per share.
